transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me today?
I came in because I keep thinking my family might be better off if I just didn’t wake up. That scared me enough that I told my supervisor, and they encouraged me to get help.
How long have you been feeling this way—thinking your family might be better off without you?
About two weeks now. It really started after my daughter left Georgia for the military.
Over these past two weeks, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even outside of thoughts about your daughter?
Yeah. I used to mess with my tomato plants, sand wood at my bench, watch the Falcons, stay after church talking with folks. Lately I just look at all that like it belongs to somebody else.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite over these past two weeks?
My appetite’s definitely changed. Most days I have to make myself eat a few bites. Even food I normally like just sits there until I end up throwing it out.
Over these past two weeks, have you been feeling unusually worthless, guilty, or like you're a burden to others, beyond just missing your daughter?
Yeah. I keep replaying her leaving and thinking I must’ve failed her somehow. Like if I’d been a better father, maybe I would’ve done something different.
Would you say these feelings of sadness and worthlessness are with you most of the day, every day, even during moments when you're not specifically thinking about your daughter leaving?
Yeah, it’s there most of the day. Even when I’m not thinking directly about her leaving, I still feel like I failed her somehow—like a better father would’ve done something different.
When you have these thoughts that your family would be better off without you, have you thought about how you might act on that, or made any plans?
I haven’t made any plans. But I keep thinking my family might be better off if I just didn’t wake up. That scared me enough that I told my supervisor.
Have these feelings and lack of energy made it hard for you to keep up with your job or daily responsibilities over these past two weeks?

Yeah. At work I’ve been making mistakes, serious enough that my supervisor found me sitting in my truck before dawn and got occupational health involved. At home, I’ve let bills and other responsibilities pile up instead of taking care of them like I normally do.
